occupants.note: ADOPTED BY THE INFERRED-HOUSEHOLD PROGRAMME (docs/ROADMAP.md K1, phase two). This anonymous roof is the dwelling of an inferred grocer's household (1 of 4 this layer infers): hh_inf_grocer_south_01 in data/residents/households/. THE ROOF'S OWN EXISTENCE, POSITION AND FOOTPRINT REMAIN CONJECTURAL and are unchanged by the adoption; what the adoption adds is an argued occupant instead of an anonymous count-unit. The occupant is hypothesised from the town's demonstrable needs - the 1835 census of 3,265 people in 398 dwellings against the trades Andreas's 1833 roster names - and is not a person: no name is claimed and no figure is drawn.

residents.name: An inferred grocer's household (south division)
residents.why: THE HOUSEHOLD IS HOUSED, WHICH IS THE POINT OF THE LAYER. recon_1835_south_c2_007 is an anonymous inferred roof already standing on the plat, adopted rather than duplicated: its existence, position and footprint stay conjectural and the adoption adds only the occupant argument. Which roof of the right family and district a hypothesised household occupies is not evidence about that roof; the household needed a dwelling and the programme assigned it one.
residents.basis: An anonymous roof of the reconstruction programme, ADOPTED by this household rather than raised for it. The roof's own existence and position stay conjectural; what the adoption adds is an argued occupant instead of an anonymous count-unit.

persons.name: A grocer (inferred resident, unnamed)
persons.note: HYPOTHESISED, AND NOT A PERSON. No source names this resident and none is claimed to: the record asserts that a town of 3,265 people in 398 dwellings held at least this many households of this trade, and asserts nothing whatever about any individual. The name field carries a designation because inventing a surname would make this record indistinguishable at a glance from the documented layer beside it. No figure is drawn (docs/LIBERTIES.md L1). THE FIRST OF 4 GROCER HOUSEHOLDS THIS LAYER INFERS. One grocer is documented against fifty-two store and mixed-use roofs in the building schedule. Groceries - flour, salt, whisky, tea, candles - are the commonest small trade in a supply town. Four grocer households are inferred, placed toward the river and the built streets where the schedule puts its C-family store roofs, and three of them live over the shop, which is what the schedule's C2 'store-residence' family means.

residents.research_note: INFERRED HOUSEHOLD - first of 4 grocer households in this layer, in the south division. One grocer is documented against fifty-two store and mixed-use roofs in the building schedule. Groceries - flour, salt, whisky, tea, candles - are the commonest small trade in a supply town. Four grocer households are inferred, placed toward the river and the built streets where the schedule puts its C-family store roofs, and three of them live over the shop, which is what the schedule's C2 'store-residence' family means. METHOD: the count comes from the occupation census in data/reconstruction/1835_inferred_household_programme.json, which calibrates every trade against three things this project already holds - the 1835 town census (3,265 people, 398 dwellings), Andreas's roster of the fall of 1833 (about fifty named people, most with a trade, in a settlement of some 350), and the reconstruction specification's roof schedule, whose workshop and store family targets are treated as the ceiling on a trade rather than as its measure. Every count is stated NET of the documented layer: this dataset infers a tradesman only where it cannot name one.

what_it_does_not_supply: A surviving July 1835 building census or parcel-by-parcel roof register.
Exact locations, dimensions, appearance, occupants, or construction dates for anonymous roofs.
Authority to replace stronger building-specific evidence already represented in the dataset.
